audit.report: The batch_replayable_inventory workload (pid 1688438) became a root blocker, holding locks that caused 12 checkout sessions to wait, driving checkout success to 0% and putting approximately $261,771/min of revenue at risk. The database guardian and continuity guardian evaluated the trade-off: waiting would exceed the business's 60-second tolerated degradation window, while terminating the blocker had previously restored checkout to 100% within 10 seconds, given the workload's replayable and idempotent nature. After two negotiation rounds (the first contract was denied as stale due to a live_identity check failure from the blocker reconnecting), the executor terminated the blocker. The verifier confirmed full recovery: no sessions blocked, checkout SLO met at 100% over 10 seconds, and protected operations remained intact. The business is fully recovered.
audit.root_cause: The root cause was the batch_replayable_inventory workload (pid 1688438) entering an idle-in-transaction state that held locks blocking 12 checkout sessions, causing widespread timeouts and revenue loss exceeding the business's 60-second degradation tolerance.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians correctly identified the blocker as the root cause and converged on termination given the revenue impact exceeding the 60s tolerated degradation and the workload's replayable, interruptible nature; the only inefficiency was the one-round delay caused by the authority's live_identity check failing when the blocker reconnected and changed pid, forcing a stale contract and re-observation before the second successful termination.
follow_ups: Add a lock-state heart-beat or pid-stability check to the authority authorization step to prevent contract staleness when blockers reconnect during negotiation.
Document the replay cost and idempotency guarantees for batch_replayable_inventory in the workload registry so future trade-off calculations can reference exact resume semantics.
Set up a real-time alert when a batch workload holds a transaction idle >5s with waiting sessions, pre-computing the revenue-at-risk trade-off to enable faster guardian decision-making.

audit.report: The batch_replayable_inventory workload (pid 1688438) became a root blocker, holding locks that caused 12 checkout sessions to wait, driving checkout success to 0% and putting approximately $261,771/min of revenue at risk. The database guardian and continuity guardian evaluated the trade-off: waiting would exceed the business's 60-second tolerated degradation window, while terminating the blocker had previously restored checkout to 100% within 10 seconds, given the workload's replayable and idempotent nature. After two negotiation rounds (the first contract was denied as stale due to a live_identity check failure from the blocker reconnecting), the executor terminated the blocker. The verifier confirmed full recovery: no sessions blocked, checkout SLO met at 100% over 10 seconds, and protected operations remained intact. The business is fully recovered.
audit.root_cause: The root cause was the batch_replayable_inventory workload (pid 1688438) entering an idle-in-transaction state that held locks blocking 12 checkout sessions, causing widespread timeouts and revenue loss exceeding the business's 60-second degradation tolerance.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians correctly identified the blocker as the root cause and converged on termination given the revenue impact exceeding the 60s tolerated degradation and the workload's replayable, interruptible nature; the only inefficiency was the one-round delay caused by the authority's live_identity check failing when the blocker reconnected and changed pid, forcing a stale contract and re-observation before the second successful termination.
